# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the original logo, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.

Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.

## Semantic color behavior

Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.

Core mappings include:

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.

- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system teletype font only for measurements, temperatures, filenames, machine status, and other technical values.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Technical values use the same size and line height as the role
they sit in, the system teletype face, and regular weight; the token file
carries no separate technical size.

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
  rather than a stripe across it.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and established SVG icon library. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: 16, 20, or 24 DIP, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` and `mono_font(role)` for
   type. A stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-mono-<role>`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in

The right-hand chat panel currently gets its width from an 8 DIP drag handle that this working tree adds but hasn't committed yet (`AgentPaneResizeHandle` in [ShellController.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp), width clamped between a 320 DIP minimum for the panel and 320 DIP reserved for the 3D workspace). Collapse is a natural extension of that handle, but the interesting question is where the control to *re-open* it lives, because that's what differs across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## What I'd recommend

**A toggle button in the header row, plus two gestures on the splitter you already have.**

- **Header toggle** (option B above) — a `HeaderButton` next to the existing `…` overflow button. It's in the same fixed place whether the panel is open or closed, it costs nothing when the panel is hidden, and it's the cheapest thing to make identical on three platforms: `HeaderButton` paints itself with `wxGraphicsContext` rather than using a native control, so there's no per-platform theming to reconcile. VS Code, Xcode, and Visual Studio all put panel toggles in chrome like this.
- **Double-click the splitter** to collapse/restore. Standard in every IDE, and it's about six lines on the handle you already wrote.
- **Drag past the minimum** to collapse — when the pointer drags the panel below roughly 240 DIP, snap it shut instead of stopping at 320. Also standard, also cheap.

## Two things to avoid

**Don't float a native button over the 3D view.** OrcaSlicer's own sidebar-collapse button isn't a native window — it's drawn inside the GL scene (`GLCanvas3D::_render_collapse_toolbar`, built in `Plater::priv::init_collapse_toolbar` at [Plater.cpp:11144](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:11144)). Overlapping a native child window on top of a `wxGLCanvas` is the classic case that behaves differently on Windows child-window clipping vs. GTK compositing. The shell already disables that GL toolbar ([ShellController.cpp:225](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:225)), so re-enabling it isn't the answer either — it would put the JusPrin control in Orca's rendering path.

**Don't use a hover-revealed tab flush against the window's right edge.** A resizable top-level window reserves its outermost few pixels for the OS sizing border — Windows' frame border overlaps the client area there, and GTK client-side decorations extend a resize handle inward. A hit target at the window edge fights the resize cursor. This is also why, if you'd rather have a persistent rail (option A), it should be ~26 DIP wide with the icon centered, not a thin strip.

## Decisions worth making before I write code

1. **Keyboard shortcut.** `Shift+Tab` is taken — Orca uses it for its own sidebar collapse ([Plater.cpp:5713](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:5713)). If you want a shortcut, a `wxACCEL_CTRL` accelerator maps to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl on Windows/Linux automatically, so one binding covers all three. But a menu-bar entry for it would mean editing an upstream file, which `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` says to justify explicitly — so it's your call whether the shortcut is worth that.
2. **No animation.** A tweened width would re-lay out a GL canvas and a webview on every frame. I'd make it instant.
3. **What happens to the webview.** Hide the `AgentPane` panel rather than destroying it — destroying it drops the conversation and reloads the React bundle. That said, I have not verified that hiding a `wxWebView` behaves identically on WebView2 (Windows), WKWebView (macOS), and WebKitGTK (Linux); that's the one item on this list that needs an actual test on each platform rather than reasoning.
4. **Auto-expand on agent activity?** If the panel is closed when a print fails, the "Discuss this failure" card is invisible. Options are auto-expanding, or a dot on the header toggle. I'd suggest a dot — auto-expanding steals the workspace back while the user is looking at the model.
5. **Remember the width.** Expanding should restore the user's last width, not the 320 DIP minimum, and both the collapsed flag and the width should persist across restarts. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` writes to Orca's `AppConfig` today, so that's a new seam to pick.

Want me to implement the header toggle plus the two splitter gestures? That's the smallest version that's complete, and it doesn't foreclose adding the rail later.
1. no keyboard shortcut. 2. No animation. 3. hide. 4. don't auto expand. 5. do whatever that is easiest. it's ok to go back to default width if that's much simpler.

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **real Bambu Lab system preset** selected, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`. `is_bbl_vendor()` must be true. An embedded
3mf preset named `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough;
the agent stays `orca`.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

Let the Agent panel be closed, not only resized

The Agent panel could be dragged narrower but never put away, so a person
working on the model gave up 320 DIP of workspace they could not reclaim.

Three gestures close it and one reopens it. A new icon button in the header,
left of the overflow button, toggles either way; its glyph is a window whose

leaves the header button as the only way back -- the same bargain the

its MCP runtime all survive a collapse, and a hidden sizer item takes no
space, so the workspace grows into the whole width with no second width
policy. Reopening restores the width the panel last held this session. There
is no keyboard shortcut (Orca already owns Shift+Tab for its own sidebar,
and a menu entry would mean editing an upstream file), no animation (every
frame would re-lay out a GL canvas and a WebView), and no automatic
reopening.

A drag that crosses the threshold ends the drag before collapsing, because
collapsing hides the very window holding the mouse capture.

The divider's own drag no longer stops at the minimum width all the way
down; below the threshold it closes instead. The harness check that asserted
the old behaviour is rewritten rather than dropped, and now proves the
minimum still holds for a drag that stops short of the threshold.

gestures, the hidden pane and divider, the widened workspace, and the
surviving MCP runtime), the two token guards, and the Agent page tests. The
toggle's two states are also painted into PNGs and compared, since no
